title: Systems of Trust — Leadership Briefing
summary: Quarterly leadership briefing focused on building "systems of trust" across the platform: reliability, security, and operational primitives for private and dedicated deployments. High-level roadmap updates, recent incident postmortem takeaways, and prioritized investments in observability and cost controls. Closed with Q&A and concrete next steps for product/infra owners.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Location: All-hands Town Hall (virtual)
Attendees: leadership + companywide

Summary section (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Maya opened with context setting: focus on trustworthiness for customers — reliability, compliance, and predictable economics.
- Liam walked through infra incident and mitigations; emphasized routing fallbacks and smarter batching as mitigations.
- Zane covered security readiness (SOC2 gaps, KMS integration, audit logs).
- Sofia and Priya described product tradeoffs: dedicated vs hosted defaults and optimizing for tail latency vs unit cost.
- Q&A surfaced timing concerns for Private (on-prem) customers and asks for clearer SLO language in contracts.

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks forjoining — sorry for the slight delay, lots going on. Today we want to cover what we're calling "systems of trust" which is basically the set of investments that make our platform predictable for customers.
[00:18] Maya: Quick agenda — incident learnings, roadmap shifts, security posture, then Q&A. Liam will start with the incident summary.
[00:28] Liam: Yeah thanks. So, on June 30th we had a cascade caused by a misrouted canary which overloaded a Dedicated pool in us-west-2. That resulted in elevated tail latency for about 22 minutes and some timeouts. The short story: routing policy didn't honor the fallback priority because of a classifier config bug.
[00:52] Liam: We corrected the config, added a health-check gating, and put in an automated rollback if latency crosses the threshold. We're also rolling out a hotfix to the router.
[01:07] Devon: Just to add — the KV cache warmed slowly because of the request distribution, and our autoscaler overshot then oscillated. We're adding a leader election for batching shards to stabilize the warm-up.
[01:24] Speaker 1: Sorry can you clarify leader election for batching shards, like what that will do?
[01:29] Devon: In short, instead of all boxes trying to create batches, one will coordinate in a shard so we avoid duplicate small batches and reduce per-token cost, and that helps tail latency on cold starts. Might be a little hand-wavy, we'll post a design.
[01:43] Priya: Also we'll try two experiments: 1) prefix-KV prewarming for high-traffic routes; 2) a light quantized variant for low-cost fallbacks to keep output quality high.
[01:57] Sofia: From product side we'll change default routing policies for new customers to prefer multi-region fallbacks rather than same-region degraded nodes. That increases cross-region traffic a bit but buys availability.
[02:12] Maya: Important to note — customers care about predictability. It's not just mean latency, it's the tail. We need better SLAs wording: what we guarantee when a Dedicated pool degrades, and explicit fallback behavior.
[02:28] Zane: On security — SOC2 prep is moving along. We're still tracking two control gaps: one around privileged access reviews and another around KMS key rotation automation for Private deployments. We'll put a runbook together.
[02:44] Zane: A couple notes: audit logs for Private are now available as a beta export, but we need to make the retention configurable per-tenant. That came up in the last RFP.
[02:58] Riley Park: Is there an ETA for the retention UI? Customers keep asking.
[03:02] Zane: Quick answer — aiming for an early-alpha in Q3, so July end for internal rollout.
[03:09] Jordan Lee: On the commercial side, finance is asking for clearer SLA credit mechanics. We need a template to plug into contracts.
[03:18] Maya: Agreed, legal and finance will produce standard SLA verbiage. One ask: let's make it explicit about when fallback to hosted/free tier happens and how we bill for those tokens during a fallback.
[03:32] Speaker 2: There's also the question of Dedicated overprovisioning vs predictable throughput — how much do we reserve?
[03:39] Devon: We'll push a capacity-guarantee model with a couple options (N% reserved, burst bucket). The new model will be configurable per-account. We want to avoid heavy manual ops.
[03:52] Sofia: For the roadmap, we're shifting two priorities: observability-first (cost attribution, token-level traces) and Private deployment ergonomics (KMS, network templates). We'll push dates to the public roadmap.
[04:07] [Slides shared: roadmap heatmap — audible shuffling and reactions] 
[04:20] Priya: On the inference side — research continues on quantization and kernel selection. Early results show ~2x cost reduction on some gen tasks with negligible quality drop, but we need more evaluation sets. We'll surface evals to product.
[04:38] Audience reaction (short burst of applause)
[04:45] Attendee (hand raise): Hey quick Q, for customers on private/offline deployments, how do we handle security patches and OS-level updates?
[04:58] Zane: Good question. For private we provide patch bundles and an automated checklist. For fully air-gapped we publish signed images and a verification tool. But we do need clearer SLAs for patch cadence.
[05:15] Maya: Ok let's talk about communications cadence. Postmortem goes to leadership and impacted customers; we should also have a 30/60/90-day follow-up for remediation. Devon can own the first postmortem note.
[05:30] Devon: I'll own that, will share by Monday 2026-07-20.
[05:35] [15-minute deep-dive recorded segment — more technical detail on routing rules and autoscaler heuristics]
[20:40] Liam: A quick technical aside — we found that some of the router rules were using legacy model aliasing which mis-classified model compatibility in edge cases. We've started a migration to a stricter model compatibility matrix.
[20:54] Liam: That'll let us fall back to quantized-compatible variants when necessary. The compatibility matrix will be in the ops repo.
[21:03] Priya: Also experiments on KV cache eviction strategy — LRU was fine but we think a priority eviction based on request frequency will help hot routes.
[21:15] Audience (murmurs): "makes sense" "nice"
[21:21] Audience Q: Does this change our recommended architecture for customers building real-time chat?
[21:28] Sofia: We'll publish an updated reference architecture: recommended batching settings, caching guidance, and fallbacks. It will include code samples and expected cost ranges.
[21:41] Maya: Shifting to observability — we need token-level breakout in the console. Right now cost by route is coarse. We'll prioritize token sampling and per-request traces.
[21:56] Jordan Lee: From finance POV, better attribution will make chargebacks and showback far simpler. It's essential for enterprise renewals.
[22:05] Taylor Nguyen: Marketing will need a short one-pager on what "Systems of Trust" means for customers — we can use that for sales and website updates.
[22:12] Maya: Good — marketing + product to collaborate on a customer-facing brief.
[22:20] [Longer Q&A block — mixed internal questions about hiring, headcount, and feedback loops] 
[35:10] Audience Q: On hiring — will we pause any hiring given this quarter's spend?
[35:18] Maya: No hiring freeze; we're tightening on non-essential spend but continuing to invest in platform and reliability hires. We do have a small pause on non-customer-facing vendor spend.
[35:33] Alex Gomez: People Ops will update hiring priority docs and share with managers.
[35:38] [Cross-talk]
[36:00] Maya: Final wrap — we have concrete owners and dates. The ask to every leader: ensure your teams know the SLA language and are prepared to support the SOC/ISO readiness workshop.
[36:12] Devon: I'll post the postmortem and the remediation checklist.
[36:16] Priya: Research will hand-off experiment specs for the two quantization/caching experiments.
[36:21] Sofia: Product will publish updated roadmap and the customer brief.
[36:26] Zane: Security will schedule the readiness workshop and share the gap list.
[36:30] [Closing remarks — thanks and adjourn]
